title: Rav Chinena son of Rava of Pashrunya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: In Pesachim 76a and Chullin 112a we find that he permitted a young pigeon that had fallen into a jar of kamka, and Rava said of him: “Who is wise enough to permit a matter like this, if not Rav Chinena son of Rava of Pashrunya, who is a great man?” In Pesachim 91a we find that Rav Ukva bar Chinena of Parishna (or Pashrunya, Dikdukei Soferim) posed a contradiction to him.

notes.text: The permitted object is the young pigeon that fell into a jar of kamka, not the kamka itself. The saved Davidson Pesachim 76a whole sentence confirms the object and Rav Chinena’s patronymic.

The consulted Pesachim 91a explicitly addresses the objection to Rava. Hyman’s compressed “to him” is retained as supplied, without establishing Rav Chinena as the addressee. The exact Dikdukei Soferim place-name reading remains Hyman’s report.
